question: An otherwise healthy 76-year-old man is brought to the physician because of poor sleep for the past several years. Every night he has been sleeping less and taking longer to fall asleep. During the day, he feels tired and has low energy and difficulty concentrating. Sleep hygiene and relaxation techniques have failed to improve his sleep. He would like to start a short-term pharmacological therapy trial but does not want a drug that makes him drowsy during the day. Which of the following is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy for this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Patient has insomnia" -> "Needs pharmacological therapy" -> "Wants to avoid daytime drowsiness" -> "Suvorexant is a dual orexin receptor antagonist" -> "Suvorexant promotes sleep without significant daytime sedation" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Patient has insomnia" -> "Sleep hygiene and relaxation techniques failed" -> "Requires medication for sleep" -> "Temazepam is a benzodiazepine" -> "Temazepam can cause daytime drowsiness" -> "Not appropriate for patient" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Patient has insomnia" -> "Wants to avoid daytime sedation" -> "Zaleplon has a short half-life" -> "Zaleplon allows for sleep initiation" -> "Less likely to cause daytime drowsiness" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Patient has insomnia" -> "Flurazepam is a long-acting benzodiazepine" -> "Flurazepam can cause residual sedation" -> "Not suitable for patient" -> 75%
CHAIN: "Patient has insomnia" -> "Diphenhydramine is an antihistamine" -> "Diphenhydramine can cause sedation" -> "Not suitable for patient" -> 70%
enhanced_information: The patient has insomnia and is seeking pharmacological therapy while avoiding daytime drowsiness. Suvorexant, a dual orexin receptor antagonist, promotes sleep without significant daytime sedation, making it a suitable option. Temazepam and Flurazepam are benzodiazepines that can cause residual sedation and are therefore inappropriate. Zaleplon has a short half-life, which reduces the risk of daytime drowsiness, but it primarily aids in sleep initiation rather than maintenance. Diphenhydramine, an antihistamine, is also sedating and not suitable. Thus, the most appropriate pharmacotherapy for this patient is Suvorexant, as it aligns with his needs for effective sleep management without daytime sedation.
analysis: The patient is experiencing chronic insomnia and is seeking pharmacological treatment that does not cause daytime drowsiness. Among the options provided, Suvorexant (opc) is a dual orexin receptor antagonist that promotes sleep without significant residual sedation, making it suitable for this patient. Temazepam (opa) and Flurazepam (ope) are benzodiazepines that can lead to daytime drowsiness, which the patient wants to avoid. Zaleplon (opd) has a short half-life and is effective for sleep initiation but may not be ideal for maintaining sleep throughout the night. Diphenhydramine (opb) is an antihistamine that is sedating and also not appropriate. Given these considerations, Suvorexant is the most appropriate choice for this patient, as it aligns with his desire for effective sleep management without the risk of daytime sedation.
